note: Verified on 2026-08-26 against the Courts Administration Authority consolidation of the Uniform Civil Rules 2020 (UCR), which is the consolidated text the courts publish; legislation.sa.gov.au lists only the gazetted principal rules and amending rules (Gazette 18.5.2020 p 1392 through Gazette 12.3.2026 p 648, commencing 15.3.2026) and does not consolidate rules of court. The CAA page states that its compilations are prepared by court staff and do not constitute an official publication — for an official version, reference must be made to the rules as gazetted. UCR r 2.2 is a complete calculation-of-time rule (calendar days, trigger day not counted, extension to the next day the Registry is open) and is the only provision the period rules apply; the Legislation Interpretation Act 2021 (SA) applies to the rules subject to contrary intention (note to r 2.3) but its reckoning-of-time provision could not be verified because legislation.sa.gov.au serves the authorised PDF and RTF behind a Cloudflare challenge that blocked every fetch path, so it is recorded pending-verification and is not applied. UCR r 2.2(5), under the sub-heading 'Supreme Court and District Court', stops time running between 25 December and 1 January for filing a defence or a notice of appeal governed by Chapter 18; the defence rule is therefore split into a Supreme/District Court entry and a Magistrates Court entry. The script approximates Registry-closed days with weekends and public holidays, and every computed date carries a warning to confirm the Registry was open.

computation_provisions.citation: Legislation Interpretation Act 2021 (SA) — reckoning-of-time provision (section number not verified)
computation_provisions.summary: The Act's rules of construction apply to the Uniform Civil Rules 2020 subject to manifestation of a contrary intention (UCR r 2.3 note, referring to ss 6-20 and s 19). Its reckoning-of-time provision (commonly cited as s 44) could not be read: the current authorised version (2021.36.auth.pdf, current from 20 November 2025) and the RTF are served behind a Cloudflare challenge that rejected Firecrawl, plain HTTP and WebFetch on the checked date. No period rule applies this provision; UCR r 2.2 governs calculation of time for the rules on its own terms.

evidence.note: Landing page scraped by Firecrawl on 2026-08-26 confirms the current authorised version succeeds the historical version of 01 January 2024 - 19 November 2025; the section text itself was not retrieved. Verify through the check-south-australia-legislation workflow before relying on the Act for any computation.

computation_provisions.summary: Calculation of time fixed by or under the rules or an order of the Court, subject to manifestation of a contrary intention (r 2.2(1)): a reference to a day is a reference to a calendar day (r 2.2(2)); if time is fixed by reference to a date or event, the day of the date or on which the event occurs is not counted (r 2.2(3)); when the time for a document to be filed is fixed prospectively and would otherwise end on a day when the Registry is closed, the period is extended to end on the next day on which the Registry is open (r 2.2(4)).

evidence.method: Downloaded the Courts Administration Authority consolidated PDF (Uniform Civil Rules 2020.pdf) linked from the UCR page located by Firecrawl scrape, extracted the text and confirmed r 2.2 exactly.
evidence.version: CAA consolidation 'Current to 15 March 2026 - Uniform Civil (No 16) Amending Rules 2026' (amendment table to Amending Rules No 16, gazetted 12 March 2026 p 648, operative 15 March 2026; accessed 26 August 2026)

computation_provisions.citation: Uniform Civil Rules 2020 (SA) r 2.2(5) (Supreme Court and District Court)
computation_provisions.summary: Time does not run between 25 December and 1 January for the purpose of the period fixed by the rules for filing a defence to a claim, a response or responding affidavit to an originating application, or a notice of appeal or review governed by Chapter 18. The subrule sits under the sub-heading 'Supreme Court and District Court' and does not apply in the Magistrates Court. The table encodes the strict reading (26 to 31 December not counted); if 25 December and 1 January are also excluded the deadline falls later, so the encoded date is the earlier and safer candidate.

evidence.method: Downloaded the Courts Administration Authority consolidated PDF, extracted the text and confirmed r 2.2(5) and its court-specific sub-heading exactly.
evidence.version: CAA consolidation 'Current to 15 March 2026 - Uniform Civil (No 16) Amending Rules 2026' (accessed 26 August 2026)

period_rules.label: Defence to a statement of claim after service of the Claim documents (Supreme Court and District Court)
period_rules.trigger: Service of the Claim documents on the respondent (defendant); the day of service is not counted (r 2.2(3))
warnings: The 28 days applies unless the Court otherwise orders (r 65.1(1)); a cross claim must be filed within the time fixed for filing the defence (r 65.2(5)). The rule the caller cited, r 63.3, concerns which Claim documents must be served, not the time for a defence.

Supreme Court and District Court only: r 2.2(5) stops time running between 25 December and 1 January for a defence, and the script does not count 26 to 31 December and refuses if the last day would roll into that window — if 25 December and 1 January are also excluded the deadline is later, so the computed date is the earlier and safer candidate. Use the Magistrates Court entry for that court.
Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed South Australian public holiday; r 2.2(4) turns on days the Registry is closed — confirm the Registry was open on the candidate date.
The source is the Courts Administration Authority consolidation, which the courts state is not an official publication; confirm against the rules as gazetted where the date is contentious.

period_rules.label: Defence to a statement of claim after service of the Claim documents (Magistrates Court)
period_rules.trigger: Service of the Claim documents on the respondent (defendant); the day of service is not counted (r 2.2(3))
warnings: The 28 days applies unless the Court otherwise orders (r 65.1(1)); a cross claim must be filed within the time fixed for filing the defence (r 65.2(5)).

Magistrates Court only: the r 2.2(5) Christmas exclusion is confined to the Supreme Court and District Court, so time runs through 25 December to 1 January; use the Supreme/District entry for those courts. Minor civil actions carry their own Chapter 20 procedures — confirm the claim is not a minor civil action before relying on this entry.
Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed South Australian public holiday; r 2.2(4) turns on days the Registry is closed — confirm the Registry was open on the candidate date.
The source is the Courts Administration Authority consolidation, which the courts state is not an official publication; confirm against the rules as gazetted where the date is contentious.

period_rules.label: Notice of appeal (including to the Court of Appeal) after the judgment or order appealed from, where leave is not sought
period_rules.trigger: The date of the judgment or order the subject of the appeal; time runs when the order takes effect under rr 103.2 and 182.2 (note to r 214.1(1)) and the day of the date is not counted (r 2.2(3))
warnings: The period is 21 days, not 28: r 214.1(1) applies subject to any statute or rule to the contrary; the caller's cited r 213.3 governs leave sought from an Associate Judge, Associate Justice or Judge at first instance, and where leave is sought under r 213.3 the appeal must be instituted within the later of 21 days after the judgment and 7 days after the grant or refusal of leave (r 214.1(2)), which this entry does not compute.

Time runs from when the order or judgment takes effect — on oral pronouncement in court, or on communication of its terms if pronounced other than at a hearing — and does not run where the Court delivers reasons without making orders (note to r 214.1(1)); the responsible lawyer supplies that date.

An appeal is instituted by filing a notice of appeal or notice of review in the prescribed form (r 214.2(1)); if an extension is required the appeal is instituted in the ordinary way and the notice seeks the extension (r 214.1(3)).

Supreme Court and District Court appellate proceedings: r 2.2(5) stops time running between 25 December and 1 January for a Chapter 18 notice of appeal, and the script does not count 26 to 31 December and refuses if the last day would roll into that window — if 25 December and 1 January are also excluded the deadline is later, so the computed date is the earlier and safer candidate.
Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed South Australian public holiday; r 2.2(4) turns on days the Registry is closed — confirm the Registry was open on the candidate date.
The source is the Courts Administration Authority consolidation, which the courts state is not an official publication; confirm against the rules as gazetted where the date is contentious.
